title: Effect of Balancing Data Using Synthetic Data on the Performance of Machine Learning Classifiers for Intrusion Detection in Computer Networks
summary: Tests whether balancing an intrusion-detection training set changes classifier performance, comparing oversampling against generated data on NSL-KDD and UNSW-NB15. CTGAN is trained to produce the minority-class samples the balanced sets are built from.
evidence: section 'Synthetic Data Generation Using CTGAN to Balance Data': we used CTGAN to generate synthetic samples to balance the training datasets in NSL-KDD and UNSW-NB15

title: Conditional Tabular GAN-Based Two-Stage Data Generation Scheme for Short-Term Load Forecasting
summary: Short-term load forecasting is limited by how little external feature data utilities hold, so this proposes a two-stage scheme that generates the missing features before forecasting. CTGAN is trained on the input variables and sampled to produce them, and is the generation model the scheme is built on.
evidence: section 'A. Data Generation Model: CTGAN' plus the algorithm steps 'Train CTGAN using' and 'Generate using the trained CTGAN'

title: Multi-Label Clinical Time-Series Generation via Conditional GAN
summary: Proposes MTGAN for generating time-series electronic health records, targeting the uncommon diseases existing EHR generators under-represent. CTGAN is both a baseline and the source of the mechanism: the smooth conditional matrix broadcasts CTGAN's conditional vector across a visit sequence, and real-sample selection follows CTGAN's training-by-sampling.
evidence: we adopt the idea of the conditional vector in CTGAN and broadcast this vector into a smooth conditional matrix; we sample real data that contain this target disease in any visit, following the setting in CTGAN; CTGAN also appears in the visit-level baseline table

title: Improved Thermal Comfort Model Leveraging Conditional Tabular GAN Focusing on Feature Selection
summary: Thermal comfort models are limited by small occupant-survey datasets, so this combines feature selection with generated data to enlarge the training set. CTGAN is trained on the survey data and the models fitted to its output are the ones reported.
evidence: section 'A. Synthetic Data Generation With CTGAN'; our trained models with the selected features on synthetic data by CTGAN outperformed the models in prior work

title: HAR-CTGAN: A Mobile Sensor Data Generation Tool for Human Activity Recognition
summary: Adapts conditional tabular generation to mobile sensor streams for human activity recognition, where readings are continuous but activity labels are discrete. HAR-CTGAN modifies CTGAN's generator for that setting, and the paper measures how progressively shifting other GANs toward CTGAN changes their output quality.
evidence: section 'The HAR-CTGAN Methodology': the approach utilizes the CTGAN method; we modify the generator in three degrees to progressively shift these models closer to a CTGAN

title: TUTOR: Training Neural Networks Using Decision Rules as Model Priors
summary: Trains neural networks on small tabular datasets by using decision rules as priors and synthesising extra data to train against. CTGAN is the generator its own synthesis framework is measured against.
evidence: Table IV: comparison between the performance of synthetic data generated by our framework and CTGAN

title: Synthetic Data Generation and Evaluation Techniques for Classification Tasks
summary: Surveys and measures generation methods for classification data, then evaluates the results at both data and model level. CTGAN is one of the generators run and scored.
evidence: we also evaluated CTGAN, a GAN-based method, for its performance in generating synthetic data

title: Federated Learning for Tabular Data: Exploring Potential Risk to Privacy
summary: Examines whether federated learning over tabular data leaks training records, treating tabular GANs as the class of model under attack. CTGAN is cited as a member of that class rather than run.
evidence: CTGAN appears only as citations among tabular GANs used for privacy attacks; no run is described

title: Federated Analytics With Data Augmentation in Domain Generalization Toward Future Networks
summary: Augments training data across federated clients to improve domain generalization in network analytics, using DCGAN for the generation itself. CTGAN appears in the bibliography but nowhere in the method, so the link is a reference rather than a use.
evidence: the paper generates with DCGAN; CTGAN is not named in the body, only in the reference list
